_comment: ONE principle: committed work is recoverable, uncommitted work is not.
This list is the commands that destroy work git cannot give back - the
working tree, the index, the stash - plus the two that destroy the reflog
that makes everything else recoverable.
Deliberately NOT blocked, because agents are meant to work autonomously:
commit, push (including --force), rebase (including --skip and --abort),
branch -D, merge, cherry-pick, revert. Every one of those either creates a
commit or moves a ref, and reflog can undo it. An agent that cannot finish
a rebase-and-force-push is an agent someone has to babysit, and a gate that
blocks the way OUT of a bad state (--abort, stash pop) is its own way of
losing work.
Separate from agent-hook-bypass.json on purpose: that file answers 'is this
call skipping verification', this one answers 'is this call about to lose
work'. They need different corrective messages, and one blocked list would
report a hard reset as a hook bypass - not what happened, not what to fix.
Enforced by the PreToolUse lifecycle hook this repository declares in
.mivia/mivia.toml. It deliberately does NOT extend to
scripts/agent_hook_guard.py: that gate is shared by every adapter agent
working in this tree, and widening it unilaterally could block a legitimate
recovery someone else is in the middle of.
correctiveMessage: This destroys work that was never committed, which git cannot give back - and other agents or the operator may have uncommitted work in this tree. Commit first if you need a clean state: a commit is recoverable, a discarded working tree is not. If discarding is genuinely what is wanted, say what you need and let the person at the keyboard run it.
